question.prompt: An equilateral triangle has side length \(6.\) What is the area of the region containing all points that are outside the triangle and not more than \(3\) units from a point of the triangle?

solutions.explanation:
The distance condition suggests separating outside points according to where they are closest to the triangle. A closest point is either in a side's interior or at a vertex.

If the closest point is in a side's interior, the shortest joining segment is perpendicular to that side. Points of this kind within \(3\) units form a rectangle of length \(6\) and width \(3\) outside each side.

At each vertex, the remaining nearby points form a radius-\(3\) circular sector between the two adjacent rectangles. The triangle has a \(60^\circ\) angle there, and each adjacent rectangle contributes a \(90^\circ\) angle. The sector angle is therefore
\[
360^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ
=120^\circ.
\]
The perpendiculars at the side endpoints separate the side strips from the vertex sectors. These three rectangles and three sectors cover exactly the desired exterior region and have disjoint interiors; their shared boundaries do not affect area.

The rectangles contribute \(3\cdot6\cdot3=54\). The sectors together have angle \(3\cdot120^\circ=360^\circ\), so together they have the area of one radius-\(3\) disk. Thus the required area is
\[
54+\pi\cdot3^2=\boxed{54+9\pi},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Separate side strips from vertex sectors
